surfaceForm: Brownfield Microsoft-centric ... The playbook adds an open policy plane and an open observability collector layer in front of the existing Microsoft estate; the Microsoft estate evolves at its own renewal pace.
location: ul-it-policy/technical/ch17-playbook-reading-EN.tex, Section 'Trajectory selection matrix' (sec:pr-trajectories), Table tab:pr-trajectory-detail (also Vocabulary, sec:pr-vocabulary, the Trajectory definition: 'brownfield Microsoft-centric')
proposedGenericDecision: Recast the trajectory as the role 'brownfield dominated by a single proprietary-suite incumbent' rather than naming Microsoft. The architectural point (open policy plane + open observability collector in front of the incumbent estate, incumbent evolving at its own renewal pace) holds for any dominant-vendor estate (e.g. a Google/Workspace estate, an Oracle estate).
rationale: Naming Microsoft makes the trajectory taxonomy read as bound to one vendor's product family. It is a vendor (not institution) binding, but it nonetheless prevents the playbook from being adoption-neutral. Recommend parameterizing to a vendor-role variable while keeping the architectural mechanism. Note the four-/five-profile trajectory set itself is a named design constant and should be kept.

location: ul-it-policy/technical/ch17-playbook-reading-EN.tex, Section 'Trajectory selection matrix' (sec:pr-trajectories), Table tab:pr-trajectory-detail, Brownfield Microsoft-centric row
proposedGenericDecision: Replace the implicit geographic anchor 'European' with a region-neutral characterization of prevalence, or parameterize the region. The claim 'most common starting point' can stand without binding it to one continent; if a region is needed it should be a localization variable.
rationale: 'European' silently assumes the adopting institutions sit in the EU/European higher-education landscape. This is an implicit jurisdiction/geography binding that an institution-agnostic suite document should not assume. Generalize (drop 'European') or parameterize the region.

location: ul-it-policy/technical/ch17-playbook-reading-EN.tex, Section 'Trajectory selection matrix' (sec:pr-trajectories), Table tab:pr-trajectory-detail, Brownfield hybrid row
proposedGenericDecision: Replace the US-specific Carnegie classification term 'R1' with a jurisdiction-neutral descriptor such as 'research-intensive institutions' (the descriptor already present) without the 'R1' label, which only carries meaning in the US Carnegie taxonomy.
rationale: 'R1' is the US Carnegie Classification 'Doctoral Universities -- Very High Research Activity' tier; it has no meaning outside the US system and implicitly binds the example to one country's classification scheme. 'Research-intensive institutions' already conveys the intent generically, so the 'R1' qualifier can simply be dropped.

surfaceForm: the international peer-comparison phase of this initiative depends on
location: ul-it-policy/technical/ch17-playbook-reading-EN.tex, Section 'Objectives of the playbook' (sec:pr-objectives), objective 4 'Generate a longitudinal record'
proposedGenericDecision: Replace 'this initiative' (which points to the specific originating University-of-Luxembourg programme and its planned peer-comparison phase) with a role-based formulation such as 'any cross-institutional peer-comparison exercise the adopting institution chooses to participate in', so the longitudinal record is justified independently of one named programme.
rationale: 'this initiative' silently equates the playbook with the single originating programme and presumes a specific 'international peer-comparison phase' belonging to that programme. In an institution-agnostic suite, the longitudinal-record rationale must not depend on the originating initiative's roadmap; generalize to an optional cross-institutional comparison the adopter opts into.

surfaceForm: the observability and audit trail required under data-protection obligations and, where the institution is in scope, NIS2
location: ul-it-policy/technical/ch17-playbook-reading-EN.tex, Section 'Minimum viable subset for resource-constrained institutions' (sec:pr-mvs), paragraph 'Why these waves.'
proposedGenericDecision: Keep the generic 'data-protection obligations' phrasing (already role-based). For 'NIS2', either keep it as a named normative framework (it is an EU directive cited as an example, already hedged with 'where the institution is in scope') or parameterize to the adopting jurisdiction's equivalent critical-infrastructure / cybersecurity-baseline regime.
rationale: NIS2 is an EU-specific directive; citing it as the audit-trail driver implicitly assumes an EU jurisdiction. The clause is already softened by 'where the institution is in scope', so it reads as an example rather than a hard binding. Lower-confidence: NIS2 is a legitimate named framework per project conventions and may be retained, but for full institution-agnosticism a jurisdiction variable for the local cybersecurity-baseline regime is the cleaner option.
